# Both directed products of two limbs, a zero factor giving zero

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `mul_dir_1` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Both directed products of $a b$ from one rounding, a bound below and one above, each within a step of its rounding:

$$d \le a b \le v.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`interval_mul_1`](interval_mul_1.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $d \le a b$, and $d$ is $\mathrm{RD}(a b)$ or at most 1 step of the format below it: a bound on that side of the exact value, at most 1 number of the format beyond its rounding down.
- $d = \mathrm{RD}(a b)$: the largest number of the format not above $a b$, when $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$.
- $v \ge a b$, and $v$ is $\mathrm{RU}(a b)$ or at most 1 step of the format above it: a bound on that side of the exact value, at most 1 number of the format beyond its rounding up.
- $v = \mathrm{RU}(a b)$: the smallest number of the format not below $a b$, when $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `mul_dir_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/DirectedProd.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/DirectedProd.v), against `mul_dir_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_dir_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition mul_dir_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let '(d, v) := mul_dir_1 emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec d /\
  fmt emin prec v /\
  d <= (a * b) /\ pred radix2 (FLT_exp emin prec) (RD emin prec (a * b)) <= d /\
  (((a * b) = 0 \/ bpow radix2 (2 * prec - 1) * eta emin <= Rabs (a * b)) -> d = RD emin prec (a * b)) /\
  (a * b) <= v /\ v <= succ radix2 (FLT_exp emin prec) (RU emin prec (a * b)) /\
  (((a * b) = 0 \/ bpow radix2 (2 * prec - 1) * eta emin <= Rabs (a * b)) -> v = RU emin prec (a * b)).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a$ is a number of `T` or an infinity, not a NaN.
- $b$ is a number of `T` or an infinity, not a NaN.

and then:

- If an operand is a zero: $d$ is a zero, whatever the other operand, $\pm\infty$ included ($0 \cdot \infty = 0$, the product of two bounds in interval arithmetic).
- If every operand is finite: $d \le a b$, and $d$ is at most 1 step of `T` below the largest number of `T` not above $a b$, which is $\Omega$ when $a b > \Omega$ and $-\infty$ when $a b < -\Omega$ (a step below $-\Omega$ gives $-\infty$).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN and none is a zero: $d = a b$, as `T` computes it.
- If an operand is a zero: $d$ is a zero, whatever the other operand, $\pm\infty$ included ($0 \cdot \infty = 0$, the product of two bounds in interval arithmetic).
- If every operand is finite and $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$: $d$ is the largest number of `T` not above $a b$, or $-\infty$ when $a b < -\Omega$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN and none is a zero: $d = a b$, as `T` computes it.
- If an operand is a zero: $v$ is a zero, whatever the other operand, $\pm\infty$ included ($0 \cdot \infty = 0$, the product of two bounds in interval arithmetic).
- If every operand is finite: $v \ge a b$, and $v$ is at most 1 step of `T` above the smallest number of `T` not below $a b$, which is $+\infty$ when $a b > \Omega$ and $-\Omega$ when $a b < -\Omega$ (a step above $\Omega$ gives $+\infty$).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN and none is a zero: $v = a b$, as `T` computes it.
- If an operand is a zero: $v$ is a zero, whatever the other operand, $\pm\infty$ included ($0 \cdot \infty = 0$, the product of two bounds in interval arithmetic).
- If every operand is finite and $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$: $v$ is the smallest number of `T` not below $a b$, or $+\infty$ when $a b > \Omega$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN and none is a zero: $v = a b$, as `T` computes it.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `mul_dir_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeDirectedProd.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeDirectedProd.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_dir_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Source

**Algorithm:** two_prod and the sign of its error term, both directions, a zero factor giving zero (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/mul_dir_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/mul_dir_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_prod`](two_prod.md).

```
# Both directed products of two numbers from one TwoProd (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "One
# limb"): d is the output of mul_down_1 and v that of mul_up_1, on the same two_prod, except that a
# zero factor gives the literal zero instead of the rounded product, so that 0 x = 0 for every x,
# an infinite x included: the product of two bounds of interval arithmetic. For finite operands a
# zero factor gives a zero product, so the claims of mul_down_1 and mul_up_1 already say it; the
# difference is 0 times infinity, which the claims say with zero_factor. The operands are not NaN
# (the bounds of a canonical interval never are). The constant is P = eta / (2 u^2), exact, the
# one of mul_down_1. Like mul_down_1, not constexpr in this milestone (it has an fms).

(p, e) = two_prod(a, b)
ap     = abs(p)
bd     = lt(ap, const up(eta/(2*u^2)))
ez     = eq(e, 0)
un     = and(bd, ez)
n      = lt(e, 0)
sd     = or(n, un)
pp     = pred(p)
dz     = select(sd, pp, p)
q      = lt(0, e)
su     = or(q, un)
sp     = succ(p)
vz     = select(su, sp, p)
za     = eq(a, 0)
zb     = eq(b, 0)
zz     = or(za, zb)
d      = select(zz, 0, dz)
v      = select(zz, 0, vz)
```
